title: records-of-truth-carry-one-extension-artifact
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> [TICKETME:waiting] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(no_record_path_spells_json) -> PROVED
author: CC
from_idea: none, because it is the first follow-on named verbatim in ticket 30531f6e1c5d's follow_ons field (CairnCommons/tickets/30531f6e1c5d-records-of-truth-change-only-through-the-artifact-door.json) and in Akien's design words of 2026-09-13 captured in CairnCommons/decisions/2026-09-13-records-of-truth-change-only-through-the-artifact-door.json: 'if we are going to build that, i'd say we have to rename the files. .json could become .artifact for those classes of files. then we only disallow one extension.'
owner: CC builds it; the door (cairn/tools/artifact) is the tool it rides — a TOOL has users, not owners (Law 6); the renamed records stay owned by whoever owns each record class.
pre_approval: Akien, 2026-09-13, on the parent ticket: 'approved thru PROVED RULED BLESSED FROM ON HIGH' — the ruling names both follow-ons; the parent's cast recorded them as cast 'when this ticket reaches PROVEME'. Pre-approval of THIS build is not claimed: it stands at his review queue.
intention: Every record of truth carries one extension, .artifact, so that 'is this a record?' is answerable from the filename alone and the jurisdiction, the PreToolUse gate and the commit question each collapse to one rule instead of a list of directories and basenames.
why: Law 1 (one spelling of the record set instead of a directory list re-derived by three readers), Law 4 (the deny rule becomes one line of physics — Akien: 'then we only disallow one extension'), Law 6 (the door stays the one gate; the rename is its first bulk write and proves it under load)
how: The rename is the door's first bulk write: `cairn artifact rename` per record through the door (old path absent, new path chained), readers rewritten behind a both-extensions flag first, rehearsed in a scratch clone, then one journaled act per repo committed under the hook; jurisdiction.json and bin/cmd/artifactgate collapse to one *.artifact rule; the flag is removed last.
how_first_cut: A migration that RIDES THE DOOR as its first bulk write: (1) census every spelling of a record path — measured 2026-09-13 after the door landed: 893 CairnCommons records, 433 cairn records journaled at genesis; 127 non-proof files / 322 sites in cairn, skills and bin spell .json for a record path (readers, globs, the jurisdiction, the gate); (2) `cairn artifact rename` each record through the door (verb rename, old path journaled absent, new path chained) in one journaled act per repo so the commit question passes before and after; (3) rewrite readers and globs to .artifact, the jurisdiction to one rule ({"name": "*.artifact"} per root), artifactgate to one extension check; (4) the proof is the migration itself: after it, `cairn artifact check` passes both roots, verify_chain is empty, zero record paths spell .json anywhere outside proofs, and a Write to any *.artifact is refused at PreToolUse.
falsifier: DONE when, measured by cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/test_artifact_rename.py and the live corpus: (1) zero files under CairnCommons/{tickets,troubles,decisions,slates,ideas,questions,adjudications} end in .json, and zero state/history/intention+why/validation files under cairn end in .json (find + count, both zero); (2) jurisdiction.json carries one rule per root — {"name": "*.artifact"} — and locate() answers yes for every renamed file and no for the lab, node_classes, notes; (3) both journals verify from genesis with every rename journaled (old path's last entry absent, new path chained from it) and `cairn artifact check` passes both roots; (4) every reader in the 127-file / 322-site census (measured 2026-09-13) reads .artifact: the ticket inspector, the harbor's clearance, the review queue, the session-open banner, the chart doors, the sorted/saveslate/idea doors all run green on the renamed corpus; (5) a Write/Edit/Bash redirect aimed at any *.artifact is refused at PreToolUse by one extension check. WRONG INTENT if a reader outside our repos needs .json — then the extension carried information and the rule is a directory rule. HORIZON: the outside-readers census is the first piece; if it reds, this ticket routes back before any file moves.
traces_to: Law 1 (one spelling of the record set instead of a directory list re-derived by three readers), Law 4 (the deny rule becomes one line of physics — Akien: 'then we only disallow one extension'), Law 6 (the door stays the one gate; the rename is its first bulk write and proves it under load)

watchme.enough: 1000 journaled writes after the rename with zero paths ending in .json inside the jurisdiction AND zero *.json files reappearing under the seven commons directories or the four cairn basenames (a reader or writer that still spells .json creates one, and that is the finding). Does not clear on a timer.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier naming every .json path that reappeared and the caller class that wrote it.
watchme.nexus: the who-writes-what tree — the same journal the counting learning block reads; a reappearing .json is a row that block would raise.
watchme.consumer: Akien, and the counting learning block once cast.

gates_bound: proof gate — cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/test_artifact_rename.py runs green under the tester over a scratch clone; the live-corpus counts (zero .json records, both roots pass check) are teeth over live data asserting invariants, never snapshots (memory proof-over-live-data-assert-invariants).

commit gate — every rename is journaled through the door, so the commit question (`cairn artifact check`) passes both roots before and after; an unjournaled rename is refused at commit by the hook already standing.
build gate — build_inspector reds cairn/tools/artifact until the rename proof seals; ticket_inspector reds this ticket on field drift.

feeds-back-to-origin on failure — a red outside-readers census routes this ticket back to Akien with the reader list (WRONG-INTENT clause); a red at PROVEME kicks it to BUILDME through the emit chokepoint.
children: none, because the rename decomposes into ordered pieces of ONE migration (census, dual-extension readers, rehearsal, live move, one-rule jurisdiction, flag removal) that the chart chain will lay out at BUILDME; none of them proves independently of the move, so none is a child.
depends_on: 30531f6e1c5d — the artifact door must stand at PROVED: the rename rides its rename verb and the block reads its journal and rides its probe poke.

cast_checks.assumption_check: THREE, with standing. (1) That nothing outside the two repos keys on a record's .json extension. UNMEASURED and load-bearing: the web server's panes, the review queue, `jq` in Akien's hands, and editor JSON modes all key on the extension today. Measured at BUILDME's first piece (a census of every reader of a record path OUTSIDE cairn/skills/bin, plus a question to Akien about his own hand habits) before a single file moves — if a reader outside our control needs .json, the falsifier's WRONG-INTENT clause fires and the answer is a directory rule, not an extension. (2) That the door's rename verb scales: 893 + 433 renames in one journaled act per repo, and the commit question (a sha per staged record against the journal) inside the pre-commit hook's runtime. Measured on 2026-09-13 at genesis: 893 entries journaled and verified in one act; the rename doubles that (absent + chained) and is measured in a scratch clone before the live move. (3) That the congruency lab, node_classes/, notes/, measurements/ stay OUTSIDE: the lab is derived and never a record; the other three are authored spec whose who is the commit author. jurisdiction.json says they 'enter when the rename ticket gives them the extension' — this cast decides NO: they stay .json/.md and outside the jurisdiction until Akien says a note is a record of truth. Recorded as a decision for his review, not assumed.
cast_checks.missing_check: TWO points asserted wrapped that are not. (a) Whole rename vs commons-only: cairn's four basenames (state.json, history.json, intention+why.json, validations/*.json) are already exact-name rules and gain nothing from an extension except one-rule-ness; renaming them touches 433 files and every charter reader (the congruency-lab compiler, build_inspector's component_color, the harbor's boat_owner_of). This cast chooses WHOLE — Akien's words were 'those classes of files', and a half-rule is the two-spellings drift Law 1 forbids — and records commons-only as the fallback if (2) above measures the whole move as too slow for the hook. (b) The learning: `history.json`'s shape ('the history of what is under way', Law 5) does not change; only the name does. The rename ticket does not touch the history-reach migration (ticket history-reach-feeds-a-migration) — a distinction recorded so the two do not get folded.
cast_checks.falsifier_check: DONE when, measured by cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/test_artifact_rename.py and the live corpus: (1) zero files under CairnCommons/{tickets,troubles,decisions,slates,ideas,questions,adjudications} end in .json, and zero state/history/intention+why/validation files under cairn end in .json (find + count, both zero); (2) jurisdiction.json carries one rule per root — {"name": "*.artifact"} — and locate() answers yes for every renamed file and no for the lab, node_classes, notes; (3) both journals verify from genesis with every rename journaled (old path's last entry absent, new path chained from it) and `cairn artifact check` passes both roots; (4) every reader in the 127-file / 322-site census (measured 2026-09-13) reads .artifact: the ticket inspector, the harbor's clearance, the review queue, the session-open banner, the chart doors, the sorted/saveslate/idea doors all run green on the renamed corpus; (5) a Write/Edit/Bash redirect aimed at any *.artifact is refused at PreToolUse by one extension check. WRONG INTENT if a reader outside our repos needs .json — then the extension carried information and the rule is a directory rule. HORIZON: the outside-readers census is the first piece; if it reds, this ticket routes back before any file moves.
cast_checks.collision_check: Judged over the whys. Law 5 (the repo is the state of the machine): the rename changes names, not what is under way — no collision. I-an-artifact-is-present-tense-or-past-tense-never-both.md already uses 'artifact' for a record of truth in the commons; the extension adopts that word rather than coining one (memory terms-drift-flag-coinages) — a distinction recorded, not a collision. The congruency lab is DERIVED (Akien 2026-08-06) and stays .json: giving it the record extension would make a viewing surface a record, which collides with its why; so it is excluded by construction. The harbor's crossings journal and the artifact journal both key on record paths by string — both are readers in the census and are updated in the same act. No exclusive-and-terminal collision found.
cast_checks.builder_check: A Haiku-level builder needs, and the ticket's how carries: (1) The exact list of what moves — the seven CairnCommons directories' *.json, and under cairn every state.json, history.json, intention+why.json and validations/*.json outside proofs/ — and the exact list of what does NOT (intentions-congruency-lab/, node_classes/, notes/, measurements/, learning/, proofs' fixtures). (2) The order: first the outside-readers census and Akien's answer; second the reader rewrite behind a flag reading BOTH extensions (so the corpus is readable at every commit); third the scratch-clone rehearsal timing the door's rename + the hook; fourth the live rename, one journaled act per repo, committed under the hook; fifth jurisdiction.json and artifactgate collapsed to one rule; sixth the flag removed. (3) How a rename is journaled: `cairn artifact rename <old> <new> --why` — the old path's last entry says absent, the new path's first entry chains from it (already built and proved under 30531f6e1c5d: tooth 'a rename leaves the old path absent and the new path journaled'). (4) What git sees: `git mv` semantics via the door (the door renames on disk; git detects the rename by content), one commit per repo, pushed. (5) The proof: a scratch clone with a handful of records of each class, renamed through the door, then every reader run against it — the same pattern as test_artifact_door's scratch clone.

challenge_at_birth.better_approach: Looked. Leaving .json and keeping the directory-list jurisdiction is zero work and already physics after 30531f6e1c5d — the rename buys ONE-RULE-ness, not enforcement. The smaller alternative is renaming only CairnCommons (7 directories, 893 files) and leaving cairn's four basenames (state/history/intention+why/validations) as they are, since those are already exact-name rules.
